desc: UK provider of fuel cards and payment services for fleets and businesses, operating from Crewe.
markets: Fuel card services to businesses in the UK and nearby European markets.
rationale: B2B fleet card supplier with links to motoring and fuel; hospitality value exists but marketing scale is modest.

name: Bharat Financial Inclusion
desc: Former Indian microfinance company, formerly SKS Microfinance, giving small loans to low-income women in rural India; merged into IndusInd Bank.
markets: Rural low-income borrowers in India; merged into IndusInd Bank in 2019.
rationale: Brand no longer exists after merger into a bank; no F1 rationale.
changed: Merged into IndusInd Bank in 2019

name: GAIN Capital
desc: Online foreign-exchange and CFD broker known for FOREX.com and City Index, serving retail traders and institutions, now part of StoneX.
markets: Retail trading customers across the US, UK, Asia-Pacific and Europe; owned by StoneX since 2020.
rationale: Trading brands under StoneX; forex and CFD brokers are already visible F1 sponsors, though regulation limits marketing.
changed: Acquired by StoneX in 2020

name: Movella
desc: Motion-capture and sensor-data company formed around Xsens, whose inertial sensors capture human movement for sports, animation, healthcare and robotics.
markets: Sells Xsens motion tracking sensors and software to customers in sport, entertainment, healthcare and robotics worldwide.
rationale: Sensor technology with sport and performance data uses; F1 could showcase telemetry-style products, but company finances are uncertain.

name: flatexDEGIRO
desc: Online broker, formed by flatex and DEGIRO, offering low-cost trading in shares, ETFs and derivatives to retail clients across Europe.
markets: Retail brokerage customers across Europe; listed in Frankfurt.
rationale: Consumer-facing broker active across several European markets; F1 offers pan-European reach and client hospitality.
changed: Merged with DEGIRO and renamed flatexDEGIRO in 2020

name: SpendSmart Networks
desc: US digital payments and mobile engagement company, formerly BillMyParents, that offered prepaid cards for teens and later mobile marketing tools.
markets: Prepaid card and mobile engagement customers in the United States; current operating status is unconfirmed.
rationale: Small US firm with unclear operating status and a domestic focus; no F1 rationale can be made.
changed: Renamed from BillMyParents

name: ONEOK
desc: US midstream company that gathers, processes and transports natural gas, natural gas liquids and refined products through pipelines.
markets: Customers are US producers, utilities and industrial users; listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: Pipeline operator with commodity business customers and little consumer branding; F1 relevance is weak.

name: Indian Oil Corporation
desc: India's largest oil company, with refining, pipelines, petrochemicals and the biggest fuel retail network in India, under government control.
markets: Mainly India, with subsidiaries in Sri Lanka and the Middle East and overseas upstream stakes.
rationale: Large fuel and lubricant brand seeking visibility; F1 could help consumer branding and India interest, but state ownership limits spending.

name: Caturus
desc: Houston-based Kimmeridge-backed natural gas company covering production and liquefied natural gas export development in the United States.
industry: natural gas producer and LNG developer
markets: US gas production and LNG export development; sells mainly to international LNG buyers.
rationale: Energy producer with no consumer brand and a US-only focus; F1 relevance is limited for this business.

name: Constellation Energy
desc: US energy company and its country's largest producer of carbon-free electricity from nuclear plants, selling power to businesses and homes.
markets: Customers are US utilities, businesses and households; spun out of Exelon in 2022; listed on Nasdaq.
rationale: US power producer selling to corporates; F1 offers some hospitality and sustainability messaging, but its market is entirely domestic.
changed: Spun off from Exelon in 2022

name: Energy Transfer
desc: US midstream energy company owning large pipeline networks for crude oil, natural gas, natural gas liquids and refined products.
markets: Customers are US producers, refiners and exporters; units trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: Pipeline operator with no consumer brand and US-only customers; F1 exposure offers little benefit to it.
changed: Energy Transfer Partners merged into Energy Transfer in 2018

name: MPLX
desc: US midstream energy partnership formed by Marathon Petroleum, owning pipelines, terminals and processing assets moving crude oil and refined products.
markets: Customers are mainly Marathon Petroleum and other US producers and refiners; units trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: Midstream partnership with captive parent customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Reliance Industries
desc: Indian conglomerate with oil refining and petrochemicals, retail through Reliance Retail, and digital services and telecom through Jio.
markets: Strong consumer base in India; exports refined products and petrochemicals worldwide; expanding in new energy.
rationale: Brand-led Indian conglomerate with Jio and retail brands and global ambitions; F1 fits its international and technology positioning.

name: Saudi Aramco
desc: State-controlled Saudi oil and gas company and the world's largest crude producer, with refining, chemicals and fuels marketing businesses.
markets: Supplies crude and products to customers across Asia, Europe and the Americas, with refining and chemicals assets abroad.
rationale: Already a long-term F1 global partner, with Aramco branding on the series, so renewal and activation are the main questions.
f1: Aramco is an F1 Global Partner (long-term championship partner)

name: Targa Resources
desc: US midstream company operating gas gathering and processing plants, liquids pipelines, fractionators and export terminals, mostly in the Permian Basin.
markets: Customers are US producers and exporters; shares trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
rationale: Midstream operator with commodity business customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Adura
desc: Joint venture of Equinor and Shell combining their UK North Sea oil and gas assets into a single independent producer.
industry: North Sea oil and gas producer
markets: UK offshore oil and gas production sold into the commodity market; formed from Equinor and Shell UK assets.
rationale: North Sea producer with no consumer brand; any F1 link would run through its shareholder Shell.
changed: Formed in 2025 from Equinor and Shell UK North Sea assets
f1: Co-owner Shell is an F1 Global Partner

name: AltaGas
desc: North American energy infrastructure company with natural gas utilities in the US, plus propane export terminals and midstream assets.
markets: Utility customers in the US and Canada, with propane exports to Asian buyers; listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
rationale: Regulated utility and midstream operator with little consumer branding; limited F1 case.

name: BB Energy
desc: London-based energy trading company offering oil product trading, operations, chartering and logistics services.
markets: Physical oil trading with customers in several regions; exact markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Trading house with a business-to-business profile; hospitality might serve clients, but the marketing case is modest.

name: Borr Drilling
desc: Offshore drilling contractor owning and operating a modern fleet of jack-up rigs for oil majors and national oil companies.
markets: Rigs work in the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Mexico, West Africa and the North Sea.
rationale: B2B drilling contractor serving oil majors; F1 hospitality could aid client relations, but marketing spending is modest.

name: Canadian Natural Resources
desc: One of Canada's largest independent oil and natural gas producers, with oil sands, conventional and natural gas operations.
markets: Production mainly in Western Canada, sold into North American and global commodity markets; listed on TSX and NYSE.
rationale: Commodity producer with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality is the only real draw.

name: Centalion
desc: Geneva-based energy trading firm active in oil and gas, per its Crunchbase description.
markets: Based in Switzerland; trading counterparties and markets are not confirmed.
rationale: Small trading firm with a B2B profile; hospitality could help but F1 is not an obvious fit.

name: Cheniere Energy
desc: Largest US liquefied natural gas producer, operating the Sabine Pass terminal in Louisiana and the Corpus Christi terminal in Texas.
markets: Exports LNG from the US Gulf Coast to buyers across Europe, Asia and Latin America.
rationale: Global LNG exporter selling to energy majors and utilities; F1 offers hospitality and energy-transition messaging, but no consumer brand.

name: CNX Resources
desc: Natural gas producer in the Appalachian Basin, including the Marcellus and Utica shales, listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
markets: Gas production in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio sold to US markets.
rationale: US gas producer with no consumer brand and a regional footprint; F1 has little relevance.

name: Commonwealth LNG
desc: Proposed 8.4 million tonne per year liquefied natural gas export project in Cameron, Louisiana, developed by Kimmeridge-backed interests.
markets: US Gulf Coast export project; offtake contracts are with international buyers. No consumer operations.
rationale: Single project vehicle with no brand to market; F1 partnership is very unlikely.
